The rocket engine was capable of producing gas temperatures in the range of 1100 to 3100°C (2000 to 5600°F) at pressures up to 4.1 MPa (600 psi).
The maximum gas temperature during the first thermal transient in the HPFTP was predicted to reach approximately 1750°C.
The heat transfer coefficient at the leading edge of an HPFTP blade was predicted to have a maximum value of 383 kW/m^2 K during steady-state operation.
The area blockage ratio for the rocket engine was 2.875, giving an area reduction at the throat of 0.348.
Significant temperature differences were observed between the three center test positions in the rocket engine, with position 4 being the hottest.
The steady-state gas temperatures increased approximately 140°C for a 10% increase in the oxidizer to fuel (O/F) ratio from 1.0 to 1.1.
The maximum near-surface metal temperature measured on an uncoated Mar-M246+Hf tube was 1310°C, in good agreement with the melting point of the alloy.
Thermal barrier coatings with thicknesses ranging from 0.011 to 0.024 cm were tested on Mar-M246+Hf tubes.
The surface roughness of the as-sprayed thermal barrier coatings was approximately 9.6 μm (377 μin.) and was reduced to 4.1 μm (163 μin.) after sanding.
